metadata.description: A Unique name used for the Virtual Machine domain and also for generating resource names. Defaults to a value prefixed with "aiovm-".
Type of authentication to use on the Virtual Machine. SSH key is recommended.
SSH key or password for the Virtual Machine. SSH key is recommended.
The size of the VM, at least 16GB RAM is required

variables.$fxv#0:
#cloud-config

write_files:
  # 1. Initial MOTD
  - path: /etc/motd
    owner: root:root
    permissions: '0644'
    content: |
      +------------------------------------------------------------+
      |          Azure IoT Operations Dev VM Provisioning          |
      +------------------------------------------------------------+
      | Status: Waiting to start...                                |
      | Script will start after boot completes                     |
      |                                                            |
      | If setup doesn't start automatically:                      |
      | $ sudo bash /root/provision_ops_vm.sh                      |
      |                                                            |
      | To watch progress in real-time:                            |
      | $ watch cat /etc/motd                                      |
      +------------------------------------------------------------+

  # 2. Improved provisioning script with non-interactive GPG handling
  - path: /root/provision_ops_vm.sh
    owner: root:root
    permissions: '0700'
    content: |
      #!/bin/bash

      # Enable error handling
      set -e

      # Set non-interactive mode for apt
      export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

      # Set up logging
      LOG_FILE="/var/log/aio-provision.log"
      exec > >(tee -a ${LOG_FILE}) 2>&1

      echo "========================================================"
      echo "Starting Azure IoT Operations provisioning at $(date)"
      echo "========================================================"

      # Total number of steps
      TOTAL_STEPS=12

      # Function to update status
      update_status() {
        local step_num="$1"
        local status_msg="$2"
        shift 2
        local details=("$@")

        {
          echo "+------------------------------------------------------------+"
          echo "|          Azure IoT Operations Dev VM Provisioning          |"
          echo "+------------------------------------------------------------+"
          echo "| Status: Step $step_num of $TOTAL_STEPS - $status_msg"
          echo "|"

          for detail in "${details[@]}"; do
            echo "| $detail"
          done

          echo "|"
          echo "| To watch progress in real-time: $ watch cat /etc/motd"
          echo "+------------------------------------------------------------+"
        } > /etc/motd
      }

      # Function to set final status
      final_status() {
        local status="$1"
        local msg="$2"
        shift 2
        local details=("$@")

        {
          echo "+------------------------------------------------------------+"
          echo "|          Azure IoT Operations Dev VM Provisioning          |"
          echo "+------------------------------------------------------------+"
          echo "| Status: $status"
          echo "| $msg"
          echo "|"

          for detail in "${details[@]}"; do
            echo "| $detail"
          done

          echo "+------------------------------------------------------------+"
        } > /etc/motd
      }

      ##### Step 1: Set up repositories - FIXED FOR GPG TTY ERROR #####
      update_status "1" "Setting up repositories" \
        "Adding package sources for Microsoft and Kubernetes"

      echo "Adding Microsoft repository..."
      wget -q https://packages.microsoft.com/config/ubuntu/24.04/packages-microsoft-prod.deb
      dpkg -i packages-microsoft-prod.deb
      rm packages-microsoft-prod.deb

      echo "Adding Kubernetes repository..."
      curl -fsSL https://pkgs.k8s.io/core:/stable:/v1.32/deb/Release.key | apt-key add -
      echo "deb https://pkgs.k8s.io/core:/stable:/v1.32/deb/ /" > /etc/apt/sources.list.d/kubernetes.list

      ##### Step 2: Install packages #####
      update_status "2" "Installing packages" \
        "Waiting for package manager..." \
        "This may take several minutes" \
        "Track detailed progress: $ sudo tail -f $LOG_FILE"

      # Wait for any apt locks
      echo "Waiting for apt locks to be released..."
      while fuser /var/lib/dpkg/lock >/dev/null 2>&1 || fuser /var/lib/apt/lists/lock >/dev/null 2>&1 || fuser /var/cache/apt/archives/lock >/dev/null 2>&1; do
        echo "Waiting for locks to be released..."
        sleep 5
      done

      # Update and install packages with proper error handling
      echo "Updating package lists..."
      apt-get update -y || { 
        echo "Failed to update package lists, retrying..."; 
        sleep 10; 
        apt-get update -y; 
      }

      update_status "2" "Installing packages" \
        "Installing core packages" \
        "This may take several minutes" \
        "Track detailed progress: $ sudo tail -f $LOG_FILE"

      apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends docker.io || { 
        echo "Failed to install docker.io, retrying..."; 
        sleep 10; 
        apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends docker.io; 
      }

      # Install Azure CLI using the improved method
      echo "Installing Azure CLI prerequisites..."
      apt-get install -y apt-transport-https ca-certificates curl gnupg lsb-release

      echo "Adding Azure CLI repository..."
      mkdir -p /etc/apt/keyrings
      curl -sLS https://packages.microsoft.com/keys/microsoft.asc | \
        gpg --dearmor | tee /etc/apt/keyrings/microsoft.gpg > /dev/null
      chmod go+r /etc/apt/keyrings/microsoft.gpg

      AZ_DIST=$(lsb_release -cs)
      echo "Types: deb
      URIs: https://packages.microsoft.com/repos/azure-cli/
      Suites: ${AZ_DIST}
      Components: main
      Architectures: $(dpkg --print-architecture)
      Signed-by: /etc/apt/keyrings/microsoft.gpg" | tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/azure-cli.sources

      apt-get update -y

      echo "Installing Azure CLI..."
      apt-get install -y azure-cli || {
        echo "Failed to install azure-cli, retrying...";
        sleep 10;
        apt-get install -y azure-cli;
      }

      apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends kubectl || { 
        echo "Failed to install kubectl, retrying..."; 
        sleep 10; 
        apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends kubectl; 
      }

      apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends git wget curl jq gnupg || { 
        echo "Failed to install utilities, retrying..."; 
        sleep 10; 
        apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends git wget curl jq gnupg; 
      }

      ##### Step 3: Ensure Docker is running #####
      update_status "3" "Starting Docker service" \
        "Ensuring Docker daemon is running"

      systemctl enable docker
      systemctl start docker

      # Wait for Docker to be ready
      echo "Waiting for Docker to be ready..."
      for i in $(seq 1 30); do
        if docker info >/dev/null 2>&1; then
          echo "Docker is ready!"
          break
        fi
        if [ $i -eq 30 ]; then
          echo "ERROR: Docker failed to start properly after 30 seconds"
          final_status "FAILED" "Docker service failed to start" \
            "Check Docker status: sudo systemctl status docker" \
            "See logs: journalctl -u docker" \
            "To view live status updates: $ watch cat /etc/motd"
          exit 1
        fi
        echo "Waiting for Docker ($i/30)..."
        sleep 1
      done

      ##### Step 4: Install K3d #####
      update_status "4" "Installing K3d" \
        "Setting up Kubernetes cluster manager"

      curl -s https://raw.githubusercontent.com/k3d-io/k3d/main/install.sh | bash

      if ! command -v k3d >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "ERROR: k3d installation failed"
        final_status "FAILED" "Failed to install K3d" \
          "Check the log for details: $LOG_FILE" \
          "To view live status updates: $ watch cat /etc/motd"
        exit 1
      fi

      ##### Step 5: Install Helm #####
      update_status "5" "Installing Helm" \
        "Setting up Kubernetes package manager"

      curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/helm/helm/master/scripts/get-helm-3 | bash

      if ! command -v helm >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "ERROR: Helm installation failed"
        final_status "FAILED" "Failed to install Helm" \
          "Check the log for details: $LOG_FILE" \
          "To view live status updates: $ watch cat /etc/motd"
        exit 1
      fi

      ##### Step 6: Configure environment and detect VM's resource group #####
      update_status "6" "Detecting Azure resources" \
        "Identifying the VM's resource group and location"

      export MYUSER=$(id -un 1000)
      export MYHOME=$(eval echo ~$MYUSER)
      export MYWORK="/workspaces"

      # Log in to Azure using managed identity
      echo "Logging into Azure with managed identity..."
      az login --identity || {
        echo "ERROR: Failed to login to Azure using managed identity"
        final_status "FAILED" "Azure login failed" \
          "Check if the VM has a managed identity assigned" \
          "To view live status updates: $ watch cat /etc/motd"
        exit 1
      }

      # Get VM metadata
      echo "Getting VM metadata..."
      VM_METADATA=$(curl -s -H Metadata:true --noproxy "*" "http://169.254.169.254/metadata/instance?api-version=2021-02-01")

      if [ -z "$VM_METADATA" ]; then
        echo "ERROR: Failed to retrieve VM metadata"
        final_status "FAILED" "Could not retrieve VM metadata" \
          "Check if VM has access to metadata service" \
          "To view live status updates: $ watch cat /etc/motd"
        exit 1
      fi

      # Extract resource group, subscription ID, and location from metadata
      export SUBSCRIPTION_ID=$(echo $VM_METADATA | jq -r '.compute.subscriptionId')
      export RESOURCE_GROUP=$(echo $VM_METADATA | jq -r '.compute.resourceGroupName')
      export LOCATION=$(echo $VM_METADATA | jq -r '.compute.location')
      export VM_NAME=$(echo $VM_METADATA | jq -r '.compute.name')
      export RESOURCE_NAME="${VM_NAME}-k8s"

      # Update status with detected values
      update_status "6" "Detected Azure environment" \
        "Subscription ID: $SUBSCRIPTION_ID" \
        "Resource Group: $RESOURCE_GROUP" \
        "Location: $LOCATION" \
        "VM Name: $VM_NAME" \
        "K8s Resource Name: $RESOURCE_NAME"

      # Set Azure subscription context
      az account set --subscription $SUBSCRIPTION_ID

      ##### Step 7: Create K3d cluster #####
      update_status "7" "Creating K3d cluster" \
        "Setting up lightweight Kubernetes cluster" \
        "Cluster name: k3s-default" \
        "Exposing ports: 1883, 8883, 8884" \
        "This may take a few minutes..." \
        "Track detailed progress: $ sudo tail -f $LOG_FILE"

      # Check if cluster already exists and delete if it does
      if k3d cluster list 2>/dev/null | grep -q k3s-default; then
        echo "Removing existing k3s-default cluster..."
        k3d cluster delete k3s-default
      fi

      # Create the cluster
      k3d cluster create k3s-default \
        -p '1883:1883@loadbalancer' \
        -p '8883:8883@loadbalancer' \
        -p '8884:8884@loadbalancer' \
        --registry-create k3d-registry.localhost:127.0.0.1:5000 \
        --wait || {
          echo "ERROR: Failed to create K3d cluster"
          final_status "FAILED" "Failed to create K3d cluster" \
            "Check the log for details: $LOG_FILE" \
            "To view live status updates: $ watch cat /etc/motd"
          exit 1
        }

      ##### Step 8: Configure kubectl #####
      update_status "8" "Configuring kubectl" \
        "Setting up Kubernetes command-line tools" \
        "Creating .kube directory for user: $MYUSER"

      # Set up kubectl config for both root and the regular user
      mkdir -p /root/.kube
      k3d kubeconfig get k3s-default > /root/.kube/config
      chmod 600 /root/.kube/config

      mkdir -p "$MYHOME/.kube"
      k3d kubeconfig get k3s-default > "$MYHOME/.kube/config"
      chown -R "$MYUSER:$MYUSER" "$MYHOME/.kube"
      chmod 600 "$MYHOME/.kube/config"

      # Verify kubectl works
      echo "Testing kubectl connection..."
      kubectl get nodes || {
        echo "ERROR: kubectl cannot connect to the cluster"
        final_status "FAILED" "kubectl configuration failed" \
          "Check the log for details: $LOG_FILE" \
          "To view live status updates: $ watch cat /etc/motd"
        exit 1
      }

      ##### Step 9: Connect K8s to Arc #####
      update_status "9" "Connecting to Azure Arc" \
        "Command: az connectedk8s connect" \
        "Resource Name: $RESOURCE_NAME" \
        "Resource Group: $RESOURCE_GROUP" \
        "Location: $LOCATION" \
        "This may take several minutes..." \
        "Track detailed progress: $ sudo tail -f $LOG_FILE"

      # Add Azure extensions
      echo "Adding Azure extensions..."
      az extension add --upgrade --name connectedk8s --yes

      # Connect to Arc
      az connectedk8s connect \
        --name "$RESOURCE_NAME" \
        --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" \
        --location "$LOCATION" || {
          echo "ERROR: Failed to connect Kubernetes to Azure Arc"
          final_status "FAILED" "Failed to connect to Azure Arc" \
            "Check the log for details: $LOG_FILE" \
            "To view live status updates: $ watch cat /etc/motd"
          exit 1
        }

      ##### Step 10: Create storage account #####
      # Generate unique storage account name
      UNIQUE_HASH=$(echo "$VM_NAME-$SUBSCRIPTION_ID" | md5sum | head -c 8)
      STORAGE_ACCOUNT="stiot${UNIQUE_HASH}"
      STORAGE_ACCOUNT=$(echo "$STORAGE_ACCOUNT" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')

      update_status "10" "Creating Azure storage account" \
        "Command: az storage account create" \
        "Storage Account: $STORAGE_ACCOUNT" \
        "Resource Group: $RESOURCE_GROUP" \
        "Location: $LOCATION"

      az storage account create \
        --name "$STORAGE_ACCOUNT" \
        --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" \
        --location "$LOCATION" \
        --enable-hierarchical-namespace true \
        --sku Standard_LRS || {
          echo "ERROR: Failed to create storage account"
          final_status "FAILED" "Failed to create storage account" \
            "Check the log for details: $LOG_FILE" \
            "To view live status updates: $ watch cat /etc/motd"
          exit 1
        }

      # Get storage account ID
      SA_ID=$(az storage account show --name "$STORAGE_ACCOUNT" --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" --query id -o tsv)

      # Generate unique schema registry name
      SCHEMA_REGISTRY="sriot${UNIQUE_HASH}"
      SCHEMA_REGISTRY=$(echo "$SCHEMA_REGISTRY" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')

      update_status "10" "Creating Azure schema registry" \
        "Command: az iot ops schema registry create" \
        "Schema Registry: $SCHEMA_REGISTRY" \
        "Resource Group: $RESOURCE_GROUP" \
        "Namespace: default" \
        "Storage Account ID: $SA_ID"

      echo "Adding IoT Ops extension..."
      az extension add --upgrade --name azure-iot-ops --yes

      az iot ops schema registry create \
        --name "$SCHEMA_REGISTRY" \
        --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" \
        --registry-namespace "default" \
        --sa-resource-id "$SA_ID" || {
          echo "ERROR: Failed to create schema registry"
          final_status "FAILED" "Failed to create schema registry" \
            "Check the log for details: $LOG_FILE" \
            "To view live status updates: $ watch cat /etc/motd"
          exit 1
        }

      ##### Step 11: Initialize IoT Operations #####
      update_status "11" "Initializing IoT Operations" \
        "Command: az iot ops init" \
        "Cluster: $RESOURCE_NAME" \
        "Resource Group: $RESOURCE_GROUP" \
        "Using --no-tls for local dev environment" \
        "This may take up to 10 minutes..." \
        "Track detailed progress: $ sudo tail -f $LOG_FILE"

      az iot ops init \
        --cluster "$RESOURCE_NAME" \
        --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" \
        --no-tls || {
          echo "ERROR: Failed to initialize IoT Operations"
          final_status "FAILED" "Failed to initialize IoT Operations" \
            "Check the log for details: $LOG_FILE" \
            "To view live status updates: $ watch cat /etc/motd"
          exit 1
        }

      ##### Step 12: Create IoT Ops instance #####
      SR_ID=$(az iot ops schema registry show --name "$SCHEMA_REGISTRY" --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" --query id -o tsv)
      INSTANCE_NAME="${RESOURCE_NAME}-instance"

      update_status "12" "Creating IoT Ops Instance" \
        "Command: az iot ops instance create" \
        "Instance Name: $INSTANCE_NAME" \
        "Cluster: $RESOURCE_NAME" \
        "Resource Group: $RESOURCE_GROUP" \
        "Schema Registry ID: $SR_ID" \
        "Configuration: Low profile (frontend: 1, backend: 1, RF: 1)" \
        "This may take several minutes..." \
        "Track detailed progress: $ sudo tail -f $LOG_FILE"

      az iot ops instance create \
        --cluster "$RESOURCE_NAME" \
        --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" \
        --name "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
        --sr-resource-id "$SR_ID" \
        --broker-frontend-replicas 1 \
        --broker-frontend-workers 1 \
        --broker-backend-part 1 \
        --broker-backend-workers 1 \
        --broker-backend-rf 1 \
        --broker-mem-profile Low || {
          echo "ERROR: Failed to create IoT Ops instance"
          final_status "FAILED" "Failed to create IoT Ops instance" \
            "Check the log for details: $LOG_FILE" \
            "To view live status updates: $ watch cat /etc/motd"
          exit 1
        }

      # Wait for IoT Ops to be ready
      update_status "12" "Waiting for IoT Ops to be ready" \
        "Checking pod status..." \
        "This may take a few minutes..." \
        "Track detailed progress: $ sudo tail -f $LOG_FILE"

      # Wait for all pods to be in Running state
      RETRIES=0
      MAX_RETRIES=20
      while [ $RETRIES -lt $MAX_RETRIES ]; do
        NON_RUNNING=$(kubectl get pods -A | grep -v "Running\|Completed" | grep -v "^NAMESPACE" | wc -l)
        if [ "$NON_RUNNING" -eq "0" ]; then
          echo "All pods are running or completed!"
          break
        fi
        echo "Waiting for pods to be ready... ($RETRIES/$MAX_RETRIES)"
        kubectl get pods -A | grep -v "Running\|Completed" | grep -v "^NAMESPACE"
        RETRIES=$((RETRIES+1))
        sleep 30
      done

      ##### Finalize #####
      # Create workspace directory
      mkdir -p "$MYWORK"
      chown -R "$MYUSER:$MYUSER" "$MYWORK"

      # Display final success message with environment details
      final_status "SETUP COMPLETE!" "Your Azure IoT Operations environment is ready to use" \
        "Environment Details:" \
        "- Resource Group:   $RESOURCE_GROUP" \
        "- K8s Resource:     $RESOURCE_NAME" \
        "- Storage Account:  $STORAGE_ACCOUNT" \
        "- Schema Registry:  $SCHEMA_REGISTRY" \
        "- IoT Ops Instance: $INSTANCE_NAME" \
        "" \
        "Useful commands:" \
        "- kubectl get pods -A" \
        "- kubectl get broker -A" \
        "- k9s"

      echo "========================================================"
      echo "Azure IoT Operations provisioning COMPLETED at $(date)"
      echo "========================================================"

  # 3. Run now script
  - path: /root/run_now.sh
    owner: root:root
    permissions: '0700'
    content: |
      #!/bin/bash
      echo "Starting Azure IoT Operations provisioning..."
      bash /root/provision_ops_vm.sh &> /var/log/manual-provision.log &
      echo "Started provisioning script in background"
      echo "Monitor progress with: tail -f /var/log/manual-provision.log"
      echo "Or monitor progress with: watch cat /etc/motd"

  # 4. Systemd service file with your change (removed cloud-final.service dependency)
  - path: /etc/systemd/system/aio-provision.service
    owner: root:root
    permissions: '0644'
    content: |
      [Unit]
      Description=Azure IoT Operations Provisioning
      After=network-online.target

      [Service]
      Type=simple
      ExecStart=/bin/bash /root/provision_ops_vm.sh
      User=root
      StandardOutput=journal+console
      StandardError=journal+console
      Restart=on-failure
      RestartSec=10s

      [Install]
      WantedBy=multi-user.target

runcmd:
  # Create directory for apt keyrings if it doesn't exist
  - mkdir -p /etc/apt/keyrings
  # Wait for a moment to ensure basic services are up
  - sleep 30
  # Start the service
  - systemctl daemon-reload
  - systemctl enable aio-provision.service
  - systemctl start aio-provision.service
